card.title: Mirror formula — where concave mirrors put images

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A concave mirror converges parallel rays to its focus (f = R/2); convex always diverges. Real images form where rays actually meet (projectable on screen); virtual images where reflected rays only SEEM to meet behind the mirror (erect, unprojectable). Position decides everything: beyond C → diminished real between F and C; at F → image at infinity.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (Cartesian: distances from pole, incident light left-to-right)  ·  f = R/2  ·  magnification m = −v/u = h_image/h_object (− = inverted real, + = erect virtual)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Paraxial rays only (near the principal axis) — wide beams suffer spherical aberration and the formula blurs. Sign convention must stay consistent through the whole solution (Cartesian recommended: u negative for real objects, f negative for concave).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Object at F of a concave mirror → reflected rays parallel → image at infinity (torch/searchlight principle, NEB 2023). Object at C → image at C, same size, inverted. Convex mirror: image always virtual, erect, diminished, between P and F (vehicle mirrors).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Object 30 cm before a concave mirror, f = 10 cm (Cartesian: u = −30, f = −10): 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/10 + 1/30 = −2/30 → v = −15 cm — real image 15 cm in front; m = −v/u = −(−15)/(−30) = −0.5: inverted, halved (NEB 2022, 4 marks).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The formula is a paraxial approximation — large apertures need parabolic mirrors. It locates the image but says nothing about brightness or aberrations. Sign-convention slips (mixing real-is-positive with Cartesian) are the top mark-killer, not physics.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From two similar-triangle pairs (object/image heights against pole, and against focus): hᵢ/hₒ = v/u and hᵢ/hₒ = (v−f)/f for concave → v/u = (v−f)/f → vf = uv − uf → divide by uvf: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. The focus-at-infinity case drops out: u = f makes 1/v = 0.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Memorise the six object positions and their images (infinity→F; beyond C→F–C diminished; C→C same; F–C→beyond C magnified; F→infinity; P–F→behind, erect magnified). Sign first, numbers second — fix Cartesian signs before touching the calculator.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): why an object at F images at infinity + what happens at C. NEB 2022 (4): 30 cm object, f = 10 cm concave — image position, magnification, nature. Real-vs-virtual differentiation repeats.
